what: No registry crate had a front-end image on a real daemon (80 of 80 refused on a hello-world, measured by lane reth-1112): `nameres::frozen`'s encoder took an OUT_DIR's text up to its FIRST `/build/` as a checkout's build directory, and blaze's default target directory is `<home>/build/<name>-<id>`, so the whole home was the place and every fetched source (`<home>/sources/..`) was a file below it.
whys: The encoder guessed which directory is one checkout's from the text of a path, by a marker (`/build/`) that the home's own layout also uses.
It had to guess because hir-def was told no directories: the build's named roots (blaze-usercode's `Roots`, blaze-cargo's `Places`) reached the database only as a one-way `Port::ported` for keys.
The fetched-sources directory was no named root at all, so nothing could write a registry path portably or say that a path was under it.
Every test of the codec used fixture paths (`/first/target/out`) with no `/build/` in them, so the layout a daemon really has was never encoded once in a test.
class: A property of a directory (whose it is) guessed from a path's text where the owner of the layout already has it by name.
prevention: The port is the one place a record asks about directories: `base_db::Port` gained `placed` (the inverse) and `held` (the one searcher, `Roots::embedded`), `Role::Sources` is a root of every build's `Places`, and the codec writes a literal's paths with the port and refuses bytes that still hold a root by the root's name. Tests use the daemon's real layout (`<home>/sources/registry/..`, `<home>/build/<id>/debug/build/<pkg>/out`).
cost: every registry crate resolved from source by every daemon, every start
fix: Written 2026-11-12 by records-1112f, not compiled or run by it: the last `/build/` of an OUT_DIR, the port's roots for the rest.
